one_line: Pala emperor of Bengal and the Śailendra ruler of Suvarnadvipa linked through a Buddhist endowment to Nalanda.

appearance.age_look: Devapala appears as a dignified man in his early 40s with a sturdy, athletic build; Balaputradeva appears as a poised man in his mid-30s with a lean, graceful build.
appearance.face: Devapala has an oval face, medium-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly groomed short beard and moustache, calm but commanding eyes with a steady gaze, and a default expression of composed authority; Balaputradeva has a slightly longer face, warm brown complexion, fine straight nose, clean-shaven jaw, expressive sharp eyes, and a default expression of diplomatic warmth and alert intelligence.
appearance.hair: Devapala’s hair is black, pulled back into a small topknot at the back of the crown, with the rest cropped short and partially hidden by a simple golden band-style coronet; Balaputradeva’s black hair is long and straight, tied into a high, smooth topknot secured with a narrow gold-and-red headband, with a short, tidy tail falling to the nape.
appearance.costume: Devapala wears an 9th-century eastern Indian royal outfit: a wrapped lower garment like a knee-length dhoti in deep red cotton with a subtle gold border, pleated neatly at the front and tied at the waist; over his upper body he wears a long-sleeved, thigh-length, front-open cloth coat inspired by early Pala depictions, in muted cream with narrow red piping, worn closed with a simple cloth tie, fully covering his torso; a broad gold-trimmed red sash crosses diagonally from his right shoulder to his left hip, and another sash girds his waist; his jewellery is restrained—two thin gold armlets, a single medium-width gold bracelet on the right wrist, a simple round gold pendant on a cord, and small round gold earrings; his feet are in plain brown leather sandals. Balaputradeva wears a 9th-century Śailendra court ensemble: a wrapped lower garment like a sarong reaching to the ankles in deep indigo with a fine repeating pattern of lighter blue and gold stripes, tied securely at the waist with a broad golden-yellow sash; his upper body is covered by a fitted, long-sleeved tunic in soft light blue cotton that reaches mid-thigh and is slit at the sides for movement, decorated with a narrow gold trim at collar, cuffs, and hem; a second indigo sash with subtle geometric motifs is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and tucked at the right hip; he wears modest jewellery—a slim gold collar necklace, small spiral gold earrings, and one thin gold armlet on each arm; his feet are in simple dark-brown sandals suitable for travel.
appearance.signature: Devapala carries a sheathed straight sword at his left hip with a plain steel blade, a simple slightly curved iron crossguard, and a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, while Balaputradeva carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with red cord in his left hand as a symbol of the Nalanda grant request.

ref_desc: Devapala is a medium-brown, oval-faced, bearded man in a cream long-sleeved coat, red dhoti, red-gold sashes, simple coronet and sword, while Balaputradeva is warm-brown, clean-shaven, long-haired in a topknot, in light-blue tunic, indigo sarong, gold-yellow sash and carrying a rolled palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two 9th-century rulers standing side by side: Devapala is a dignified, medium-brown man in his early 40s with an oval face, calm commanding eyes, neatly groomed short beard and moustache, and black hair pulled into a small back topknot under a simple golden band coronet; he wears a fully covering cream long-sleeved, thigh-length front-open cloth coat with narrow red piping, tied closed, over a knee-length deep-red dhoti with subtle gold border pleats, a broad red-and-gold sash from right shoulder to left hip, another sash at the waist, restrained gold armlets, bracelet, round pendant, small gold earrings, and plain brown sandals, carrying at his left hip a sheathed straight sword with simple iron crossguard and dark-brown leather scabbard. Balaputradeva is a poised, warm-brown man in his mid-30s with a slightly longer face, sharp expressive eyes, clean-shaven jaw, and long black hair tied into a high smooth topknot with a short tail, secured by a narrow gold-and-red headband; he wears a fully covering light-blue long-sleeved fitted tunic to mid-thigh with gold trim at collar, cuffs, and hem, an ankle-length deep-indigo patterned sarong with fine light-blue and gold stripes tied by a broad golden-yellow sash, a second indigo sash draped from left shoulder to right hip, slim gold collar, small spiral earrings, thin armlets, and dark-brown sandals, holding in his left hand a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with red cord; emphasise clear, consistent face shapes, hairstyles, garments, sashes, sword and manuscript, and a harmonious palette of deep red, cream, gold, indigo and light blue.
